description: #3892 — the three value-shape arms of `filtered_blocks_query_inner`'s per-filter dispatch that had never been exercised, plus the key-presence arm that has no value predicate at all. Before #3892 the ratchet keyed on the COMMAND, and `filtered_blocks_status_open` (the `valueText` arm, in `query_reads_links_search_pages`) made the whole command read as covered while `valueTextIn` / `valueDate` / `valueDateRange` / no-value emitted SQL nothing had ever compared across the two stacks. Every step below is authored to fail for a SPECIFIC reason a plausible implementation gets wrong (set membership vs first-element, date column vs text column, half-open vs closed range, key-scoped EXISTS vs any-property EXISTS) rather than to pin one obvious row. The first four steps use non-reserved keys; a reserved key (`todo_state` / `priority` / `due_date` / `scheduled_date`) routes to a direct `b.<col>` predicate instead of an EXISTS over `block_properties` — a second dispatch dimension the first four steps deliberately do not mix in. #3930 review note 2 — that second dimension was credited with zero differential evidence (every step above uses a non-reserved key, so the reserved-column routing at `queries.rs`'s `reserved_col` match ran only under `filtered_blocks_status_open`'s non-reserved arm, never its own). `filtered_reserved_key_presence_only` below drives it directly: a bare key-presence filter on `todo_state`, which for a reserved key emits ONLY `AND b.todo_state IS NOT NULL` — the sole predicate gating that arm.

blocks.content: no status, due on the exclusive upper bound

name: query_filtered_blocks_value_shapes

queries.comment: #3892 `valueTextIn` arm — `value_text IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?N))`. Discriminating because BOTH members must match: an implementation that compared against the first element only (or that bound the JSON array as a scalar) returns a strict subset. S5/S6 own a `due` but no `status`, so they must be excluded — the EXISTS is key-scoped, not block-scoped. #3976 — S7 is the NEGATIVE CONTROL and the reason this step can fail at all: it carries `status = "archived"`, a value OUTSIDE the IN list, so the membership predicate is the only thing that excludes it. Without S7 every block holding the key also held a listed value, and deleting the IN test returned the identical set (measured: the mutated predicate was green across the whole frontend suite).
queries.name: filtered_value_text_in_matches_either_member

queries.comment: #3892 `valueDate` arm — `value_date = ?N`. Discriminating because the value lives in the `value_date` column, not `value_text`: an implementation that compared the wrong typed column returns nothing at all. S5's `2026-08-15` and S6's `2026-08-16` are near misses on the same key.
queries.name: filtered_value_date_exact

queries.comment: #3892 `valueDateRange` arm — `value_date >= ?from AND value_date < ?to`, a HALF-OPEN interval. Both bounds are pinned by a row: S2 sits exactly on `from` (an exclusive lower bound drops it) and S6 sits exactly on `to` (an inclusive upper bound admits it). S3's `2026-09-20` is far outside.
queries.name: filtered_value_date_range_is_half_open

queries.comment: #3892 the fifth arm: NO value predicate, so the EXISTS degrades to mere key presence (`property_value_predicate_sql` returns an empty fragment). Discriminating because S4 owns a property — just not this one — so an EXISTS that dropped the `bp.key = ?` predicate, or one that required a value, gets a different set.
queries.name: filtered_key_presence_only

queries.comment: #3930 review note 2 — the reserved-column counterpart of `filtered_key_presence_only`. `todo_state` is a RESERVED key, so this filter routes to the direct `b.todo_state` predicate (`queries.rs`'s `reserved_col` match) instead of an EXISTS over `block_properties`, and with no value field supplied the only predicate that arm emits is `AND b.todo_state IS NOT NULL`. Discriminating because B2 (via S2) is the only block with a `todo_state` set — an implementation that dropped that gate, or that fell through to the non-reserved EXISTS branch instead of the reserved one (which would look for a `block_properties` row keyed `todo_state` and find none), returns a different set than just B2.
queries.name: filtered_reserved_key_presence_only
